builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Instant Weight-Space Consolidation for Long-Term Memory in LLMs
summary: It replaces agentic text-extraction memory pipelines and serving-time fine-tuning with a recurrent hypernetwork that compiles session activations into a low-rank adapter in a single forward pass, plus a fixed-size episodic buffer. Cost is a trained hypernetwork and per-session forward passes with fixed memory footprint, but the method requires training or obtaining the consolidation hypernetwork and validating it on the reader's models and memory workloads. It can fail where consolidation loses verbatim detail, where cross-session patterns are sparse, or where distribution shift makes the pre-trained hypernetwork underperform text retrieval.
rationale: The approach fits constrained infrastructure because it eliminates serving-time backpropagation and generative consolidation calls, but its gains are demonstrated on specific benchmarks and models, so production adoption requires workload-specific validation.
technique: Gradient-free weight-space consolidation for long-term LLM memory

claims.statement: It replaces agentic text-extraction memory pipelines and serving-time fine-tuning with a recurrent hypernetwork that compiles session activations into a low-rank adapter in a single forward pass, plus a fixed-size episodic buffer. Cost is a trained hypernetwork and per-session forward passes with fixed memory footprint, but the method requires training or obtaining the consolidation hypernetwork and validating it on the reader's models and memory workloads. It can fail where consolidation loses verbatim detail, where cross-session patterns are sparse, or where distribution shift makes the pre-trained hypernetwork underperform text retrieval.

On LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S with 2-7B models, CLAM leads agentic memory baselines by 1-45 points and gradient-based parametric methods by 10-45 points; the consolidated adapter adds 12-15 accuracy points when the episodic buffer misses the gold evidence and 4-5 points with an oracle buffer, while requiring zero generative calls, zero gradient steps, and 3-151x less wall-clock time to build memory.
